name: Authored change → validate it with the OpenSpec CLI oracle
description:
The validate station (R6, group 6 — now a publish-triggered COMPONENT). `validate` is a SUB-STEP of the OpenSpec lifecycle, not a coordinator taxonomy action, so no coordinator decision routes it — instead this rule chains off the authored marker. When an authoring loop calls create_change, the tool stamps openspec.change.authored=<slug> on THAT loop entity (the slug-independent signal; the run's own facts are slug-namespaced and no rule condition can wildcard-match them). This rule fires on that marker and fires a plain `publish` to component.validation-station.dispatch — the VALIDATION STATION component hydrates the change from the run's facts, shells `openspec validate <slug> --strict --json --no-interactive` in a temp dir, and — from the real exit code (G3) — stamps openspec.validated on the run (pass) or clears it (fail), with ZERO model turns (validate replaced its forced coordinator loop, R6). The existing run-lifecycle/01-offer-change-approval gate then advances executing→awaiting_approval.

WHY IT FIRES ON THE LOOP + passes TWO properties: this rule fires on the authoring LOOP entity (that is where openspec.change.authored lives), which carries agent.run (inherited via create_change's run_scope=inherit). The rule engine's executePublish stamps the dispatch entity_id = the LOOP (the firing entity) — but the validation station needs the RUN. So the publish threads BOTH the run_entity_id ($entity.triple.agent.run.entity_id) and the slug ($entity.triple.openspec.change.authored) as properties; the station reads them from the dispatch. (Contrast the projection station, which fires on the run and needs no run property.)

MECHANISM: the validation station calls the SAME validatechange.Validate core the old tool used (one writer of openspec.validated, G5). It stamps the marker's VALUE = the content revision (D15 #0), so a re-author is detected. A CLI REJECT clears the marker (the gate cannot advance) — a definitive verdict, not a retry.

No openspec.validated guard: the rule fires on the LOOP marker, and openspec.validated lives on the RUN — not readable from the firing loop entity. Edge-triggering (fire-once on the authoring loop via RULE_STATE) is the re-fire guard; a rework re-author is a NEW loop entity, a legitimate fresh trigger (D5/D15#0: a re-author re-validates, idempotently). KNOWN M0 GAP (honest, general to all R6 stations): a persistent oracle-unrunnable transport fault (after the station's bounded retry) leaves the change unvalidated with nothing re-triggering — no auto-park at M0 (R8/group 8).

metadata.station: validation-station — run the OpenSpec CLI oracle on the authored change (R6 component)
metadata.trigger: openspec.change.authored on the authoring loop entity (create-change-author-tool stamps it; slug-independent so a rule can match it).
metadata.mechanism: R6: a plain `publish` to component.validation-station.dispatch triggers the validation STATION component (zero model turns), replacing the forced validate_change coordinator turn. Fires on the authoring LOOP, so run_entity_id + slug travel as publish properties (the firing entity is the loop, not the run). Emitted on core NATS (the rule component declares no matching JetStream output port).
metadata.advances: openspec.validated on the run → run-lifecycle/01-offer-change-approval fires executing→awaiting_approval.
metadata.known_gap: general R6 station gap (honest): a persistent oracle-unrunnable fault after the station's bounded retry leaves the change unvalidated with no auto-park at M0 — reconciled by R8/group 8.
